The "Edit profile" page ships with two bugs. The name field is empty even though the profile clearly loaded, since the page title shows the user's name. The bio box is empty too, and the first letter typed into it prints a console error: "A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled." Both fields were written as if
were interchangeable ways to fill an input, and both read their starting values on the first render, before the profile request had finished.

Smart developers hold it because controlled inputs are what most tutorials teach first, and the pattern is genuinely useful. It also looks true on screen: on the first render,

content.text: Make a field controlled when the UI needs its value while the user is typing: a character counter, a submit button that enables itself, validation on every keystroke, a live preview, or a second field that depends on the first. Keep it uncontrolled when its value only matters at submit time. React 19 makes that case pleasant: pass a function to
and it receives the form's data, and after the action succeeds React resets every uncontrolled field in the form.

A controlled input re-renders the component that owns its state on every keystroke, along with everything below it. React's docs suggest moving the input and its state into a small component of its own so the rest of the page stays still. If the big tree really depends on the text,
